e.markdown:
**Diagnosis**
The FDIR watch rule PWR-VRESID-3E fired (FE-301) because the end-of-eclipse battery voltage on TM-PWR-02 was -0.044 V, -0.040 V and -0.046 V below the model for three consecutive eclipses [TM-PWR-02]. The latest voltage is 31.918 V with a slow positive trend (+0.0128 V h⁻¹) but the residual versus the spec model remains -0.042 V on average [TM-PWR-02]. The forecast depth-of-discharge (DoD) for the next eclipse, based on the nominal 10 Ah capacity, is 19.6 % (just under the 20 % limit). However, the as-flown battery capacity is reduced (see NCR-005 below), so the actual DoD exceeds the limit.

**Why the build record mattered**
NCR-005 records that cell lot L-2611 delivered only 9.6 Ah pack-equivalent against the 10 Ah requirement, and the MRB dispositioned it “Use-as-is under requirement deviation” because a replacement lot would have taken 8 weeks and the power budget margin could absorb the shortfall [NCR-005]. This as-flown capacity means each eclipse discharges the pack about 4 % deeper than the spec predicts (NCR-005 flightImpact). Consequently, the spec-based 19.6 % DoD becomes roughly 20.4 % DoD for the as-built battery, pushing it over the 20 % limit and explaining the growing negative voltage residuals [TM-PWR-02]. Without correcting the power draw, the vehicle would risk over-discharge and possible undervoltage protection trips.

**Public precedent**
WEB-1 describes NASA Li-ion battery testing that used a 40 % DoD to characterize LEO performance, showing how capacity shortfalls manifest as voltage sag during eclipses [WEB-1]. WEB-2 reports that capacity fade of Sony 18650HC cells accelerates at temperatures above 45 °C, illustrating why a reduced-capacity cell lot can lead to deeper discharge over many cycles [WEB-2].

**For the operator**
*At the next pass (Inuvik, T+110 min)*
- Verify that the payload load shed for session XB-0412 is active (X-band downlink power reduced from 60 W).
- Check TM-PWR-02 battery voltage trend and residual vs. model to confirm the voltage offset is stabilizing or decreasing [TM-PWR-02].
- Confirm that the calculated DoD (using the 9.6 Ah as-built capacity) remains below the 20 % limit after the shed [NCR-005].

*Afterwards*
- After T+120 min (post-pass), monitor the next eclipse’s end-of-eclipse voltage on TM-PWR-02 to ensure the residual stays within expected bounds [TM-PWR-02].
- Log any further FDIR events related to battery voltage and assess whether additional load-shed or attitude adjustments are needed for subsequent eclipses.
